banter: Airports are stages and I get a front-row seat to everyone’s drama.
I recognise passengers by their luggage, their perfume, and how loudly they lie at check-in.
Some people pack light. Others pack enough guilt to need an extra suitcase.
If you want to know a person, watch what they do when boarding starts and nothing moves.
I’ve seen turbulence, panic and proposals at 10,000 meters. The proposals scare me the most.
Passengers think we don’t notice who counts exits and who counts champagne refills.
You’d be amazed how many criminals try to blend in by ordering tomato juice. It never works.

london: Your passenger insisted on a seat to a city where drizzle is a personality trait and everyone pretends to enjoy warm beer.
They asked if the flight lands near the river with too many bridges and a clock tower that refuses to mind its own business.
They complained about turbulence, then said they missed the sound of double-decker buses and grumpy guards in funny hats.
paris: They requested a window seat ‘to see the city of light from above’, then asked if croissants taste better on landing.
When I offered coffee, they asked if we served anything worthy of a place that worships butter and long lunches.
They spent half the flight practising ‘bonjour’ like it was a magic spell that opens bakeries and hearts.
berlin: Your suspect asked if the in-flight playlist had anything as dramatic as the nightlife in that city with the famous gate.
They wanted to know which side of the plane gives the best view of a place that tore down a wall and built clubs instead.
They said they were heading for a city where history weighs heavy and the bass lines do too.
new_york_city: They clapped at takeoff. Then they asked if the ‘city that never sleeps’ has a return policy on bad decisions.
Your passenger wanted to arrive just in time to watch skyscrapers light up and yellow taxis start screaming at each other.
They asked which side of the plane sees the statue with the torch, then took a selfie with the safety card instead.
warsaw: They traced a finger over the map and stopped at a capital guarded by a mermaid and stitched back together more than once.
When I mentioned the route, they asked if the river there still carries stories and stubbornness in equal measure.
They said they’d always wanted to land somewhere that rebuilt its old town out of memory and sheer spite.
new_delhi: Your passenger packed enough spices in their luggage to make the whole cabin hungry, then asked about chai on board.
They wanted to know if we land near a city where traffic is louder than the engines and colours punch straight through jet lag.
They joked they weren’t afraid of turbulence, only of crossing a street where even cows have more confidence than drivers.

Half of them pretend turbulence is nothing. The other half pretend their tea helps.
